one_month_reasoning: Inside the window to 2026-11-13: (1) Q3 2026 results on Friday 2026-11-06, 10 a.m. ET (company release of 2026-09-29, src 31). Management said on the Q2 call it expects to update 2026 and 2027 guidance then, or to wait on 2027 until Cogentrix closes. I expect 2026 at or above the $7.2B midpoint and 2027 near the $7.4B low end ex-deals (~$8.1B with Cogentrix and Meta), i.e. no upside surprise versus what the CFO already signalled; the stock fell after both earlier 2026 reports, so a modest downside skew. (2) Macro: the 2026-10-14 drop (-6.3% to $152.2) was the AI-power group selling on the hot September CPI (BLS: +0.6% m/m, core +0.3% m/m), not Vistra news (no 8-K since 2026-10-05, EDGAR); the FOMC meets Oct 27-28 (Fed calendar, src 32) with the 10-year at ~5.2%, so the rates factor sets most of the 1-month spread. The stock is whippy: it ran +20.5% from Sep 30 then fell -6.35% on Oct 8 (TIKR, src 33). Sharp factor-driven drops partly reverse about as often as they extend. (3) No PJM auction result in the window (2029/30 BRA expected December 2026; backstop procurement suspended to 2027-02-28). So a near-symmetric spread centred just below spot (~$152) at ~14% monthly vol (50%/3.5) with slightly fat tails; unchanged in substance from round 1 because the supervisor's findings confirm, not change, the window's events.

thesis_break_reason: At $112 the pro forma equity (112 x ~340.6M shares incl. the 5.0M Cogentrix shares = $38.1B) plus pro forma net debt and preferred (~$25.4B = $19.16B + $2.48B preferred + $3.8B Cogentrix cash and assumed debt) is ~$63.6B EV, ~7.85x the $8.1B 2027 base: ~1x below NRG (8.9x), the cheapest peer, and below my bear-case multiple. Reaching it outside a market-wide crash would most likely mean a fundamental break: PJM moving to cap or administratively set 2030/31+ capacity prices (no extension filed as of 2026-10-14; PJM's stakeholder evaluation runs to end-2026, then it sets the 2030/31+ path, ER26-1556 answer), 2027 guidance on Nov 6 well below $7.4B ex-deals, the Cogentrix deal failing, or a downgrade below investment grade. ~26% below spot and ~16% below the 52-week low ($132.66). I keep $112 rather than the supervisor's $115: both sit ~1x below NRG; at $115 an ordinary 1.5-sigma year with no fundamental news gets there more often.

reverse_dcf_check: The engine's reverse DCF says the multiple legs (EV/EBITDA $165, P/E $156; weighted $163.5) imply a WACC of ~8.2% with 2% terminal growth; at my 9.25% WACC they imply ~3.1% perpetual growth after FY2029 (DCF at g=3.0% = $161, at 3.25% = $170) with pre-SBC EBITDA margins held near 38.8%. 3% nominal growth forever for a merchant fleet facing a ~45% chance of a post-2030 PJM cap, ERCOT oversupply and coal retirements is generous, which is why the 2%-growth DCF ($131) carries 30% and the multiple stays below the peer median.

reasoning: Round 2. Cause of the 2026-10-14 drop (verified, unchanged): VST -6.3% to $152.2 with no 8-K or release since 2026-10-05 (EDGAR); the AI-power/AI-infrastructure group sold off on the hot September CPI (BLS: +0.6% m/m, +3.7% y/y; core +0.3% m/m), 10-year ~5.2%: sector/market-wide, not company-specific, so it does not move fair value. PJM cap status (the thesis-break trigger), as of 2026-10-14: FERC accepted the ~$175 floor / ~$325 cap collar for 2028/29 and 2029/30 on 2026-04-28 (ER26-1556); PJM's answer limits it to auctions through 2029/30 and commits to a stakeholder evaluation by end-2026 before setting the 2030/31+ path; the 2026-09-29 FERC order (ER26-3380/EL26-108) accepted and suspended the Reliability Backstop to 2027-02-28 and opened a section 206 proceeding. No filing to extend the cap exists: flag open, not tripped. What changed after the supervisor's review: (1) SBC was counted twice (after-SBC EBITDA against pre-SBC peer multiples, plus SBC shares); I confirmed at source that Talen's and Vistra's adjusted EBITDA add back stock comp, and moved to pre-SBC EBITDA with SBC as dilution only. (2) Dropped the unsupported $0.1B 2027 haircut and the thin FMP 2028 consensus; 2027 $8.1B, 2028 $8.5B by my own build. (3) Added the Cogentrix ~$0.7B tax NPV, confirmed in Vistra's release, at 0.9 probability. (4) P/E leg now on the model's own EPS. (5) PJM post-2030 cap probability 0.5 -> 0.45; I stay above the supervisor's 0.4 (see revisions). Fair value $153.9 (EV/EBITDA $165, P/E $156, DCF $131); scenarios $106/$154/$202 at 30/45/25; engine median $149.5. Skeptic findings still stand: 2027 is trending to the low end; 2028 is only ~72% hedged into lower ERCOT forwards; the balance sheet absorbs $3.8B of Cogentrix plus $1.5B of 7%+ hybrids at BBB-; BMO cut its target to $210 from $231 on Oct 5 (TIKR, context only). No short-seller report or sell rating found. Ladder: centred ~$151.7 (between the engine median and fair value, leaning to the 30% bear weight) with ~42-45% effective vol and fat tails, P(>=152) 0.495. Round-2 follow-ups: 3 web searches/fetches plus 4 primary-document checks (Cogentrix release, Talen and Vistra Q2 reconciliations, Q3 date release, Fed calendar); PJM's 2029/30 parameters PDF could not be text-extracted here, so the December BRA date stays unconfirmed.
